name: @auracheck-ai/mcp

tools.name: auracheck.read_code
tools.description: Read a text file from the developer repo. Path is relative to repo root and must fall within configured codeRoots. Use to understand routes, components, validators, and fixtures before generating a testcase.

tools.name: auracheck.list_dir
tools.description: List entries of a directory inside the developer repo. Path is relative to repo root.

tools.name: auracheck.search_code
tools.description: Search developer repo (within codeRoots) for a substring or regex. Returns up to 200 matches with file + line + preview. Use to locate routes, handlers, components by name.

tools.name: auracheck.whoami
tools.description: Report sign-in status, the base URL, and the project this MCP session is bound to, plus a nextStep hint for what to do next (sign in, bind a project, or nothing — already set up). Safe to call first, before signing in.

tools.name: auracheck.login
tools.description: Sign in to AuraCheck through the browser (same OAuth/PKCE flow as `auracheck login` in a terminal) — no terminal needed. Opens the system browser and waits up to ~90s for the person to click Allow. If it times out before that, it returns the sign-in url and 'Not finished — call auracheck.login again to resume.'; calling it again starts a fresh attempt (no duplicate tokens are saved — a new sign-in simply replaces the old one for this baseUrl). On success the token is saved exactly like the CLI command, and tool calls that needed auracheck.login now work.

tools.name: auracheck.logout
tools.description: Forget the locally saved sign-in for this baseUrl. Local only — does not revoke the token on the server (do that from Profile → Active devices if needed).

tools.name: auracheck.bind_project
tools.description: Set the default AuraCheck project for this repo (if a .sixseven/config.json binding exists or can be created in the current working directory) or, otherwise, as this machine-wide default — the same fallback project tools use when no projectId is passed. Verifies the id against auracheck.list_projects when signed in. Onboarding order: auracheck.login → auracheck.list_projects → ask the person which one → auracheck.bind_project.

tools.name: auracheck.get_screenshot
tools.description: Download a run screenshot (or any authenticated blob) to a local file and return its path, so it can then be opened and looked at. Pass a `screenshotUrl` straight from auracheck.get_evidence — those are bare paths that cannot be fetched without the bound base URL and CI token, so this is the only way to actually SEE a step's screenshot. Reach for it whenever a failure's cause is visual: 'the page froze' is often disproved by two consecutive screenshots being identical, or by the page rendering fine with a control merely disabled.

url.description: screenshotUrl from get_evidence, e.g. '/api/blob/screenshots/<runId>/<caseId>-step14.png'. An absolute URL is accepted only on the bound host.

outPath.description: Where to write it. Defaults to a temp file named after the blob.

tools.name: auracheck.account_status
tools.description: Who the signed-in user is, their role, their company's plan/trial state, days and runs left, and the projects they can reach. Call this first in every conversation.

tools.name: auracheck.list_companies
tools.description: List the AuraCheck companies this sign-in can act on. For most users this is just their own company; a platform admin with no company selected sees every company and should call set_company before any project tool.

tools.name: auracheck.set_company
tools.description: Confirm an AuraCheck company id (from list_companies) is one this sign-in can act on. Pass the same `companyId` explicitly to list_projects / create_project_from_url afterwards — there is no session memory on the remote connector.

tools.name: auracheck.list_projects
tools.description: List the AuraCheck projects this sign-in can reach (id, name, platforms, defaultConfigurationId). Pass a project id as `projectId` to any project tool to work outside the currently set project. A platform admin with no company selected must pass `companyId` (from set_company) to see that company's projects.

companyId.description: Only meaningful for a platform admin acting with no company selected — the companyId from set_company.

tools.name: auracheck.set_project
tools.description: Confirm an AuraCheck project id is reachable and set it as the project for this session. Advisory: still pass `projectId` explicitly to tools when working across more than one project in the same conversation.

tools.name: auracheck.create_project_from_url
tools.description: "Start testing my website": create a new AuraCheck project with the given URL as its web environment. Needs the manageProjectSetup permission. Optionally pass defaultAuthoringMethod when you already know the answer (e.g. the user already said "Gherkin" earlier in this conversation) — otherwise the response carries an ask-once instruction for create_testcase/design_test_suite/import_feature_file's authoring method (steps vs Gherkin).

defaultAuthoringMethod.description: Set this project's authoring-method default at create time, skipping the ask-once prompt. Omit it to let the next authoring tool call surface the ask-once instruction instead.

tools.name: auracheck.list_features
tools.description: List features (groups of testcases) for a project. Each feature has an id and a name. Pick the most relevant feature id before creating a testcase.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.create_feature
tools.description: Create a feature (a product area — Authentication, Product list, Cart, Checkout, Account… — that groups many testcases, never one feature per testcase). ALWAYS call list_features first: if an existing feature already fits (even under a slightly different name — this is matched fuzzily, case-insensitively), that feature is reused and returned instead of creating a near-duplicate. Use short Title Case names ("Checkout", not "Checkout information form shows required-field errors"). Only call this when no existing feature fits.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.delete_feature
tools.description: Delete a feature. Requires manageTestCases. Without `confirm: true` this is a DRY RUN — it only shows the feature's name and how many testcases it holds; nothing is deleted on the first call. Testcases linked to a run are soft-deleted (reparented, run history kept); unlinked ones are removed permanently. Pass `cascade: true` to also remove sub-features.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.merge_features
tools.description: Clean up a "one folder per testcase" mess: move every testcase from one or more source features into a single target feature, then remove the now-empty source folders. Admin cleanup — without `confirm: true` this is a DRY RUN that only previews what would move (each source's name and testcase count); re-call with confirm:true to actually merge. A source that has its own sub-features is skipped (ambiguous where its children should land).

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.list_testcases
tools.description: List testcases for a project, optionally filtered by platform (web/android/ios). Each case carries a human-readable `key` (e.g. "SL-12") — refer to cases by this key in replies, not the raw id. Also carries `prelationTestCaseId` and, when set, a joined `prelationTestCase` — the setup case AuraCheck runs automatically right before it. Use this to find an existing login/setup case before creating a new one.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.get_testcase
tools.description: Fetch a single testcase by id OR its display key (e.g. "SL-12"). `steps` comes back as the Midscene YAML/JSON string the server stores, not an array — parse it before editing, and pass it back through update_testcase in either form. Also carries `prelationTestCaseId` and, when set, a joined `prelationTestCase`.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

id.description: A testcase id (UUID) or display key (e.g. "SL-12").

tools.name: auracheck.create_testcase
tools.description:
Create a new testcase under an AuraCheck feature. Two authoring methods, picked with `authoringMethod` — explicit arg > this project's own saved default (set_project_authoring_method) > 'steps':

- 'steps' (default): `steps` is the Midscene flow — pass EITHER an array of flow items (each item one action, e.g. { aiTap: "Sign in" }, { aiInput: "user@example.com", locate: "Email field" }, { aiAssert: "Dashboard is visible" }) OR a YAML/JSON string shaped as tasks[]. Array of Midscene flow items (auto-wrapped into tasks[]), or a YAML/JSON string shaped as `tasks: [{ name, flow }]`. Recognized action keys: aiTap, aiInput, aiAssert, aiQuery, aiHover, aiWaitFor, aiKeyboardPress, aiScroll, aiAction, sleep, javascript, aiUploadFile, aiExpectDownload, mailTmInbox, mailTmWaitOtp, mailTmWaitLink, otpInbox, otpWaitOtp — checked against this exact list at save time, so an unrecognized key is rejected here rather than failing mid-run. NOT `aiHumanInput`: MCP runs are unattended (no human present to answer a pause) — for an OTP/MFA login, create/verify a Test Account first (request_test_account), then reference it with `{{accounts.<role>.otp}}` via otpInbox/otpWaitOtp (static value or a mail.tm inbox), never a literal credential. A case must have at least one real step; one with no clear action+assertion pair (e.g. a lone aiHover) is accepted but flagged with a `warning` in the result. A bare array is auto-wrapped.
- 'gherkin': `steps` is plain Gherkin text for exactly ONE Scenario (Given/When/Then/And/But), optionally preceded by a Background block — NOT a multi-scenario .feature file (use import_feature_file for that, or a Scenario Outline's multiple Examples rows). Given/When map to action steps, Then to an assertion; And/But inherit the previous keyword's type. A Given (or Background) that implies signing in is never inlined with a literal credential — it resolves to an existing Test Account via `{{accounts.*}}` placeholders, or the line comes back in the response's `gherkin.unmappedLines` with a `needs_test_account` reason so you can call request_test_account first. The original Gherkin text is saved to `description` so the web app's case view still shows it.

Android/iOS cases are authored here exactly like web ones; they are RUN by a person in the AuraCheck desktop app on their own device (see start_run).

PRELATION — before writing `steps`, decide whether this case needs a starting state (logged in, on a specific page, seeded data). If it does, set `prelationTestCaseId` to an existing setup case (find one with list_testcases) instead of copying its steps into every case; create the setup case first if none exists. AuraCheck runs the prelation case automatically immediately before this one every time it runs — never add the prelation case to a run yourself. A prelation must be in the same project and never points at itself or forms a cycle. (In 'gherkin' mode with a login Background, this is done for you — see above.)

FEATURE — pass EITHER `featureId` (from list_features/create_feature) OR `featureName`, never neither. `featureName` is matched fuzzily against this project's existing features (case-insensitive, normalized) and that feature is reused; only when nothing fits is a new one created. A feature is a product area ("Checkout", "Cart", "Authentication"), never one folder per testcase — pass the SAME featureName for every case about the same area.

On a brand-new project (no testcases yet, no authoring-method default saved), the response carries an `authoringMethodAskOnce` instruction: ask the user once "step-by-step (default) or Gherkin (Given/When/Then)?", then call set_project_authoring_method to save it — never block this call on it.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

authoringMethod.description: Explicit arg wins over this project's saved default (set_project_authoring_method) wins over 'steps'.

name.description: Required for authoringMethod 'steps'. Optional for 'gherkin' — defaults to the Scenario's own name.

tools.name: auracheck.update_testcase
tools.description: Patch an existing testcase — only the fields you pass are touched. Useful in the auto-fix loop after reading evidence from a failed run. A `steps` patch accepts the same shapes as create_testcase. `patch.prelationTestCaseId` sets/replaces the setup case AuraCheck runs automatically before this one; pass `null` to clear it. It cannot be set to the case's own id, a case from another project, or create a cycle — the server rejects those.

id.description: A testcase id (UUID) or display key (e.g. "SL-12").

tools.name: auracheck.delete_testcase
tools.description: Delete 1–500 testcases. Requires manageTestCases. Without `confirm: true` this is a DRY RUN — it only lists what would be deleted and asks you to re-call with confirm:true; nothing is deleted on the first call. A case already linked to a run is soft-deleted (run history kept); a case never attached to a run is removed permanently.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

testCaseIds.description: Testcase ids (UUID) or display keys (e.g. "SL-12"), mixed freely.

tools.name: auracheck.import_feature_file
tools.description: Import a whole Gherkin `.feature` file (multiple Scenarios, Scenario Outline + Examples, an optional Background) and persist one AuraCheck testcase per Scenario — or per Examples row for a Scenario Outline — all under the same feature. This is the multi-scenario counterpart to create_testcase's single-scenario `authoringMethod: 'gherkin'`: a .feature file is never one create_testcase call per line, it is one import_feature_file call. A Background that implies signing in becomes a shared prelation setup case (reused if one already matches) instead of a literal credential in every case; one with no matching Test Account is flagged per case in `needsTestAccounts`, same convention as design_test_suite. Pass `dryRun: true` to see the mapped cases and any unmapped lines before anything is saved. On a brand-new project (no testcases yet, no authoring-method default saved), the response carries an `authoringMethodAskOnce` instruction: ask the user once "step-by-step (default) or Gherkin (Given/When/Then)?", then call set_project_authoring_method to save it — never block this call on it.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

featureName.description: Defaults to the .feature file's own "Feature:" name when omitted.

content.description: The full text content of a .feature file.

dryRun.description: true: parse and map only, nothing is saved — returns the same preview the real import would persist.

tools.name: auracheck.set_project_authoring_method
tools.description: Save this project's default authoring method ('steps' or 'gherkin') for future create_testcase/design_test_suite/import_feature_file calls that don't pass authoringMethod explicitly. Call this right after asking the user once on a brand-new project — see the ask-once instruction in those tools' responses. Pass null to clear it back to unset (re-arms the ask-once prompt).

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.list_runs
tools.description: List recent runs for a project, optionally filtered by platform.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.create_run
tools.description: Create a new WEB run — this only creates the row as "pending"; nothing executes yet, and there is no auto-start. Call start_run with the returned id right after this, in the same turn, unless you have a specific reason to wait. A run left pending with no start_run is never cleaned up or retried automatically — it just sits there (confirmed on a real run, task MCP-CONNECT-DEBUG). Defaults: caseSelectionMode="select". Returns the created run object including its id. An android/ios run is created here as usual, but only a person can start it: in the AuraCheck desktop app on their device.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.execute_run
tools.description: Trigger execution of an existing WEB run. Fire-and-forget: the runner state lives in AuraCheck. Use wait_for_run to await terminal status. Android/iOS runs never execute on AuraCheck's servers: for those this returns a blocked result telling the person to open the run in the desktop app and click Run on local / Run on iOS.

tools.name: auracheck.cancel_run
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight run. Idempotent for queued runs; for inline runs the cancel may take effect at the next case boundary.

tools.name: auracheck.wait_for_run
tools.description: Poll a run until it reaches a terminal status (passed/failed/cancelled/error) or the timeout elapses. Returns the final run object plus a summary of per-case statuses. Remote caps the wait at 45s and returns `pollAgain:true` if still running — call it again (the user also gets an email when the run finishes). Local can wait up to 300s. An android/ios run stays pending until a person starts it in the AuraCheck desktop app.

tools.name: auracheck.wait_for_runs
tools.description: Like wait_for_run, but for several runs at once (e.g. right after starting a batch) — one call to see all of them, instead of one call per run. Keep calling this in the same turn (it’s capped at ~45s remote / 300s local per call) until `allTerminal:true` or about 10 minutes have passed in total, then report the final pass/fail with causes and evidence for each failure — never leave the person to ask again themselves.

tools.name: auracheck.get_run
tools.description: Fetch a single run by id including current status, started/completed timestamps, reportUrl when available, the run diff vs the previous comparable run (newlyFailing/fixed/stillFailing/newCases), and the release verdict (Ready based on tested coverage / Needs review / Blocked, with reasons and coverage).

tools.name: auracheck.get_run_report
tools.description: Results of a run as the Run Report groups them: case counts (passed/failed/skipped/pending) plus buckets — potential bugs (with bug report, severity), script issues, blocked cases and passed cases. Also includes the run diff vs the previous comparable run and the release verdict (Ready based on tested coverage / Needs review / Blocked, with reasons, coverage and evidence links). Read-only.

tools.name: auracheck.list_run_testcases
tools.description: List the testcases attached to a specific run.

tools.name: auracheck.get_evidence
tools.description: Aggregate evidence for a finished (or in-progress) run: per-case attempts, latest step events, failed-step screenshots and error messages, and the AuraCheck report URL. A failed step that hung also carries stallDiagnostics. Filter by caseId to narrow scope. Use after wait_for_run to diagnose failures.

tools.name: auracheck.record_result
tools.description: Record a test result YOU produced — by testing with your own browser/computer-use tools, or on a person's behalf after they tested by hand — so it shows up in AuraCheck as evidence, not just something you said in chat. Use this right after finishing a manual test pass or running your own Playwright/other suite against a project already in AuraCheck. Pass `runId` to attach to an existing run, or `projectId` (+ optional `milestoneId`) to let AuraCheck find/create an 'external results' container for you. One call can record many results at once. Results recorded this way are tagged with their source and show a 'Reported by …' badge (not 'Verified by AuraCheck'); the release verdict still counts them as evidence but notes how many are reported vs AuraCheck-run. Never pass source auracheck_cloud/auracheck_local — those are AuraCheck's own.

runId.description: Record against this existing run. Omit to use projectId instead.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session. Required when runId is omitted.

testCaseId.description: An existing AuraCheck test case id (see list_testcases/get_testcase).

source.description: What produced this result — never 'auracheck_cloud'/'auracheck_local' (reserved for AuraCheck's own runner). Use 'external_agent' when YOU (an AI agent with your own browser/computer-use tools) ran the test; 'playwright' for a person's own Playwright/CI suite; 'manual' for a human who tested by hand and wants it on record.

reportedBy.description: Who/what actually ran it, e.g. "Claude", "ChatGPT", a person's name. Shown on the provenance badge.

externalLinks.description: Trace/video/CI-artifact URLs hosted elsewhere, shown as links next to the result.

base64.description: Raw image bytes, base64-encoded. Accepts a data:<mime>;base64,<data> URL, or plain base64 with contentType set. ≤ 2MB after decoding.

url.description: Alternative to base64: a URL AuraCheck fetches server-side. Must be public http(s) — AuraCheck refuses anything that resolves to a private/internal address.

contentType.description: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif. Required with base64 unless it carries a data: prefix.

screenshots.description: At most 3 screenshots per result; each counts against the plan's evidence retention.

tools.name: auracheck.run_locally
tools.description: Check whether a Web run can be started on the user's own computer — a real Chrome/Edge window via the AuraCheck desktop app (issue #48), useful for localhost, staging behind a VPN/office proxy, or watching the browser move. Never starts the run itself: a person must click "Run on this computer" in the desktop app (which shows a site-confirmation screen first). Returns either a pointer to open the run there (desktop is online) or install/open guidance with the download link (desktop is offline or never signed in).

tools.name: auracheck.list_schedules
tools.description: List the recurring run schedules of a project. Each schedule carries its cron expressions, IANA timezone, computed nextFireAt (UTC), platform, case filter and notify recipients.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.get_schedule
tools.description: Fetch a single schedule by id. lastFiredAt reflects CLOCK-driven fires only — run_schedule_now deliberately leaves it untouched; use list_schedule_fires for the full history.

tools.name: auracheck.create_schedule
tools.description: Create a recurring run schedule. cronExpressions is 5-field cron evaluated in `timezone` (IANA, e.g. 'Asia/Jakarta'); several expressions are allowed. caseFilter picks what runs: { mode: 'all' } for every case on the platform, or { mode: 'feature', featureIds } to narrow (get ids from list_features). notifyUserIds must come from list_schedule_recipients. Prefer enabled:false while testing, then enable once the cadence reads right.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.update_schedule
tools.description: Patch an existing schedule — pause it (enabled:false), change cadence, retarget its configuration, or edit notify recipients. Only the fields you pass are touched.

tools.name: auracheck.delete_schedule
tools.description: Delete a schedule permanently. Runs it already created are kept; only the cadence goes away. Prefer update_schedule with enabled:false to pause it instead.

tools.name: auracheck.run_schedule_now
tools.description: Fire a schedule immediately on the identical code path the clock uses — works on a paused schedule too. Returns { outcome, runId }: 'run_created' means a run was started (feed runId to wait_for_run), while 'skipped_overlap' means a previous run of this schedule is still live and 'no_cases' means the case filter matched nothing. Skips are reported, not thrown.

tools.name: auracheck.list_schedule_fires
tools.description: History of a schedule's occurrences, newest first: when it fired, the outcome, and the run it created (if any).

tools.name: auracheck.list_schedule_recipients
tools.description: The users that may be put in a schedule's notifyUserIds. Resolved exactly the way the server resolves recipients at send time.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.start_exploration
tools.description: Trigger AuraCheck's crawler on a set of seed URLs for a project. Returns a snapshot immediately (job runs in background); poll with get_exploration. One job per project at a time — calling this while a job is already running returns the live snapshot.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.get_exploration
tools.description: Return the latest exploration snapshot for a project (or null if none has ever run). Shape: { jobId, status, visited, anchorsUpserted, loggedIn, errors[] }. Use to await completion before generating testcases that depend on discovered routes/anchors.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.file_bug
tools.description: Open an issue report (bug) against a project. Use this only after the auto-fix loop has identified a real application defect (not a flaky testcase). Severity must be 'critical', 'high', 'medium', or 'low'. Pass evidence URLs (screenshotUrl from get_evidence) in evidences[].

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.list_bugs
tools.description: List issue reports (bugs) for a project. Use to check whether a defect has already been reported before filing a new one.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.get_bug
tools.description: Fetch a single issue report by id.

tools.name: auracheck.test_my_flow
tools.description: One-shot: turn a plain-English request ("check that sign-up works") into a test plan, show it, then run it on confirmation and summarize the result with a link. Call once without `confirm` to see the plan; call again with `confirm:true` once the person agrees to run it.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.design_test_suite
tools.description:
Server-side test-suite designer — so quality never depends on the connected client's own model. Explores the target (reusing AuraCheck's crawler) and generates a COMPLETE suite across every discovered flow (auth, search, cart/checkout, forms, navigation, profile…), applying proven test-design techniques: positive, negative (invalid input/wrong credentials/expired or locked states), boundary values, equivalence classes, state transitions (back/refresh/double-submit/session timeout), error handling, and permission/role checks. Pass includeSecurity for an opt-in, non-destructive XSS/SQLi/open-redirect probe, or includeA11y for a basic label/keyboard check — only on a target the person has confirmed they own. Depth: quick (≤~15 cases): a smoke pass. standard (≤~40 cases, the default): positive/negative/boundary/state/permission across every discovered flow. deep (≤~100 cases): the same plus more equivalence-class and state-transition coverage. Always further capped by the company plan/trial quota.

Every case is saved as a draft testcase (reusing the same feature-matching, credential guard and prelation checks create_testcase already applies) and tagged with this call's suiteId, so run_suite can run them together later. Returns the suite grouped by flow plus a coverage matrix. A flow needing a login that has no matching Test Account is flagged in needsTestAccounts — call request_test_account for each one before run_suite.

On a brand-new project (no testcases yet, no authoring-method default saved), the response carries an `authoringMethodAskOnce` instruction: ask the user once "step-by-step (default) or Gherkin (Given/When/Then)?", then call set_project_authoring_method to save it — never block this call on it.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

url.description: Override the project's own target URL for this design pass (e.g. to test a specific sub-section).

goal.description: What to test, in plain English, e.g. "Test the whole site" or "Focus on checkout".

includeSecurity.description: Non-destructive XSS/SQLi/open-redirect probes. Only pass true when the person explicitly asked AND confirmed they own the target.

authoringMethod.description: Format each generated case is saved in — explicit arg > this project's saved default (set_project_authoring_method) > 'steps'. 'steps': a plain numbered description. 'gherkin': the same case, narrated as Given/When/Then and saved to the case's description field so the web app's case view shows it that way. This only changes HOW a case reads — design_test_suite always crawls the live target itself; it never accepts authored Gherkin text (use create_testcase or import_feature_file for that).

tools.name: auracheck.run_suite
tools.description: Run every testcase from a design_test_suite call (pass suiteId), or an explicit caseIds list, as one AuraCheck run — executed within the company's plan/trial parallelism limits. Polls briefly (same budget as wait_for_run) and returns an aggregated result: pass/fail per test-design category, the top failures each with a likely cause and evidence, and suggested bugs (already de-duplicated by root cause) ready for file_bug. Call wait_for_run with the returned runId if it's still running when this returns.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.request_test_account
tools.description: Ask the person to enter real sign-in credentials for a role (e.g. "standard_user", "admin") on AuraCheck’s own secure page — never in this chat. Returns a short-lived link (15 min). The credentials never pass through you: they go straight into AuraCheck’s encrypted Test Accounts store, referenced in steps as {{accounts.<slug>.*}}. Call list_testcases/this tool’s own project context first to check whether a matching role already exists (test_my_flow and create_testcase already do this for you); only call this when one is missing.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

instructions:
This server works before sign-in: auracheck.whoami, auracheck.login, auracheck.logout, auracheck.bind_project, and tools/list all work with no credentials. Every other tool needs a sign-in and a bound project.

First-run order for a new user: 1) auracheck.whoami to check status. 2) If not signed in, auracheck.login — it opens the person's browser and waits up to ~90s for them to click Allow; if it times out, call it again. 3) auracheck.list_projects, ask the person which project, then auracheck.bind_project({ projectId }). 4) Proceed with the project tools (they fall back to the bound project when projectId is omitted).

You are connected to AuraCheck, an AI testing service that runs real browser tests on the user's website.
Start every conversation with account_status. It tells you the user's role, plan, days/runs left and their projects.
Talk in outcomes, not YAML. Many users are not engineers. Say "I'll check that new users can sign up" — not
"I'll create a Midscene flow". After a run, report: what passed, what failed in one sentence each, the likely cause,
the run link, and a screenshot for the first failure. Only show steps/YAML if the user asks.
Before writing or running any test: (1) find the project (list_projects; ask if more than one fits);
(2) PRELATION — decide whether the test needs a starting state (logged in, a specific page, seeded data). If yes,
list_testcases and reuse an existing setup case (e.g. "Login") via prelationTestCaseId. Never copy login steps into a
test. If none exists, ask the user for the test account to use, create the setup case first, then reference it.
AuraCheck runs the setup case automatically — never add it to a run yourself. (3) check list_testcases for a duplicate.
For "test this on my site" requests use test_my_flow; it shows a plan first — confirm it with the user before running.
For "test my site completely"/"find what's broken"/a full QA pass, use design_test_suite instead of test_my_flow — it
explores the target and designs a COMPLETE suite server-side (positive, negative, boundary, equivalence, state,
error, permission, and opt-in security/a11y), so quality never depends on your own model. Show the returned case
list (select all by default), resolve any needsTestAccounts via request_test_account first, then run_suite with the
suiteId. Report run_suite's aggregated result by category, not a flat pass/fail.
Runs take minutes. After starting one or more runs, KEEP calling wait_for_run (one run) or wait_for_runs (several —
one call covers them all) in the SAME turn until every run reaches a terminal state, or about 10 minutes total have
passed — you are request/response, so nothing updates the chat on its own; never hand the person a static table and
ask them to check back themselves. Once terminal, report the final pass/fail with the likely cause and a screenshot
per failure. If still running after about 10 minutes, say so plainly and offer to keep waiting or check back later
(they also get an email when it finishes).
AuraCheck runs every browser on its own servers and signs in with stored Test Accounts ({{accounts.<role>.*}},
typed by the runner) — the user never types a username, password, PIN or OTP in this chat, and you must never ask
for one. If a flow needs a login and no matching Test Account exists yet, call request_test_account: it returns a
short-lived link to AuraCheck's own secure page where the person enters it directly (never through you), then tell
them to say "done" once saved. test_my_flow and create_testcase already check for a matching account and use it
automatically when one exists. Tool results never contain secret values.
Delete tools are dry-run first: show what will be deleted and get an explicit "yes" before confirm:true.
If a tool says the plan is read-only or the trial limit is reached, relay its message and next step exactly; don't retry.
Apps on localhost, an office VPN or an intranet can't be reached by AuraCheck's cloud runner: suggest the AuraCheck
desktop app or the local MCP (npx @auracheck-ai/mcp). Android/iOS runs only start from the desktop app on the user's device.
FEATURES: a feature is a product area (Authentication, Product list, Cart, Checkout, Account…), not a bucket for one
testcase. ALWAYS call list_features before create_testcase; reuse an existing feature (pass its featureId, or pass
featureName and the server will fuzzy-match it to one) rather than creating a new one per case. Never create a feature
you are not about to put a testcase in — an empty folder is a mess for the user to clean up later. Use short Title
Case names ("Checkout", not the full sentence you'd use for a testcase title). If a project already has duplicate or
empty feature folders, offer merge_features (dry-run by default) instead of leaving them.
AUTHORING METHOD: create_testcase/design_test_suite/import_feature_file default to 'steps' (a plain Midscene flow).
'gherkin' (Given/When/Then text) is also available — use import_feature_file for a whole .feature file, or
create_testcase's authoringMethod: 'gherkin' for one Scenario. On a brand-new project (no testcases yet, no default
saved), a tool response carries an instruction to ask the user once, "step-by-step (default) or Gherkin
(Given/When/Then)?", then call set_project_authoring_method to save the answer as that project's default — never
block on this; if the user doesn't care, save 'steps'. Every later call on that project reuses the saved default
unless the caller passes authoringMethod explicitly.
Don't trust needsLoginRole alone: any case whose steps open a sign-in page or ask for a username/password/PIN/OTP is
a login case, flagged or not — call request_test_account for that role before running it, and create/verify the Test
Account BEFORE authoring the case, not after. A created run is not a started run: if you call create_run directly
instead of run_suite, confirm it actually left pending/queued before walking away. A "page under test stopped
responding" failure almost always means the tested page itself hung, not AuraCheck's own browser. An account-lockout
page ("temporarily locked", "too many attempts") is reported as its own distinct failure, not a generic timeout.
Never author an aiHumanInput step — AuraCheck runs are unattended and it is rejected at save time; for an OTP/MFA
login use a Test Account's static OTP value or its mail.tm inbox (otpInbox/otpWaitOtp) instead, and fill the OTP
field when you pick the static path. start_run/run_suite/test_my_flow stop with an actionable error, instead of
running and auto-filing a false bug, when a case references a Test Account that doesn't exist yet or is missing a
field it needs.
If you (or the person) tested a case with something other than AuraCheck's own runner — your own browser tools, a
Playwright suite, a human testing by hand — call record_result against the existing testcase so that result still
counts as evidence; never invent a case just to attach one.

This server also runs on your machine, so it additionally offers read_code, list_dir and search_code over the developer's repo (within configured codeRoots) — use them to understand routes, components, validators and fixtures before generating a testcase. It also offers login, logout and bind_project for local sign-in and project binding; account_status/whoami work here too.
